gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: The company has ___ enormous losses this quarter.
gaps.explanation: 'Suffer losses' is the standard collocation for experiencing financial loss.

gaps.sentence: The roads were almost empty — the traffic was surprisingly ___.
gaps.explanation: light traffic means few vehicles on the road; its opposite is heavy traffic.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ sure that all the windows are locked.
gaps.explanation: make sure means to check that something is true or has been done.

gaps.sentence: The two sides struggled to ___ an agreement before the deadline.
